originality.rationale: The primary 2026 model paper, inspected at full HTML Sections 2.3, 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3, establishes the periodic path formula and separate long-time ensemble mean and variance; it neither states a lag covariance function nor its strictly positive nonmixing plateau. The new argument proves phase mixing of products for every fixed lag, removes lag harmonics, and proves strict period-mean monotonicity through an exact coth identity. Searches of named photobioreactor/random-frequency and lag-covariance formulations and related mathematical research found no same-model positive-plateau classification. Generic dephasing and ergodic-mixture identities remain known and substantially overlap the method; novelty is asserted narrowly for the specific kinetic model and strict all-density conclusion.
residual_risks: A general quenched-frequency ergodic-decomposition theorem may subsume the generic covariance-plateau identity; value and asserted novelty reside in its strict photobioreactor specialization.
Not all older random-frequency literature or source supplementary material were exhaustively compared.
The physical source assumes a random period held fixed through each trajectory, not a fresh random period every switching event.

value.rationale: The motivating model calculated ensemble one-time mean and variance, but two-time persistence of fluctuations matters for deciding whether observed cultures forget their forcing heterogeneity. The result identifies an exact nonzero long-lag second-order signature for every continuously variable period law and all physical two-mode positive coefficients, with a constructive explicit strictly monotone mean. It distinguishes quenched period variability from per-cycle stochastic renewal; it is a motivated structural classification, not a numerical table or routine parameter substitution.
